title: Cornyn links Nvidia scandal to perception of Trump admin corruption
summary: The outgoing Texas Republican senator said “the buck stops with [Trump]” when pressed on whether the White House plays a role in the appearance of corruption and self-dealing.
content: Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn sees the Nvidia scandal and questions about the Trump administration’s alleged lax chip export control rules as part of a broader perception of corruption, which he said contributed to the Republican drubbing in the midterms. “Let’s talk about Nvidia and export controls,” the Texas Republican said when asked to name examples of corruption he sees at the federal level during an onstage interview at the Atlantic Summit on Tuesday. He then pointed to media reports that advanced Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China through the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and that the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, resisted efforts by other Cabinet agencies to crack down on Megaspeed. “I just think there’s a lot of things that will be investigated, and we’ll learn more about, basically, this perception that there was self-dealing going on that I think caused a lot of unease by the American people,” Cornyn said. He said President Donald Trump is at the center of the perceived corruption — “the buck stops with him” — and that many congressional Republicans, fearing the White House’s retribution, have chosen not to cross the president publicly. Cornyn’s remarks come as fallout from the Nvidia turmoil that led to CEO Jensen Huang’s ouster continues to roil Washington. The Trump administration is scrambling to further restrict China’s access to the most advanced American chips as pressure mounts from Capitol Hill, which is also set to hear testimony from Huang and Lutnick in the coming weeks. The four-term senator, who lost his primary earlier this year to the Trump-endorsed Ken Paxton, did not mince words when asked about the cause of the blue wave that swept even statewide offices across his home state. “Well, President Trump said he was on the ballot.” In a pair of statements, White House spokespeople blamed Democrats for refusing “to do anything to stop waste, fraud, and abuse in our government” and highlighted the Commerce Department’s interim final rule to “crack down on the smuggling of advanced U.S. SI chips, including through third countries and remote access by Chinese SI labs.” “The Trump Administration will continue to take decisive action to protect America’s technological edge, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI is built in America,” White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said. Cornyn in his remarks Tuesday also urged Washington to keep China as its top national security and foreign policy focus, as Trump is set to meet with China’s leader Xi Jinping later this week. He warned about disruption to the semiconductor supply chain should China try to invade Taiwan, its island democracy neighbor that produces an overwhelming majority of the world’s most advanced chips. “The idea that there could be another pandemic or military conflict or natural disaster that would disrupt that ought to worry everybody,” he said. “That’s one of my principal concerns is what China may or may not do in the Taiwan Straits.”
